les: Wat gaan in, en wat kom uit
kaps_punt: masjiene en toerusting benodig energie insette om hulle te laat werk; masjiene en toerusting verskaf energie uitsette (werk) wat vir ons nuttig is

items.bewering: Die ketel staan vol water op die tafel, en niks gebeur nie. Steek die prop in die muur en die ketel maak die water warm.
items.bron: Penn State EGEE 102, 'Examples of Day-to-Day Energy Transformations' (e-education.psu.edu/egee102): electrical energy into an appliance becomes heat. Note: this skips switching on at the wall and on the kettle. That is a compression, not a false claim, and it does not change the input-output point.

items.bewering: Energie moet eers by 'n masjien ingaan voordat hy kan werk. Ons noem daardie energie wat by hom ingaan, die inset. Masjiene, toestelle en toerusting het almal 'n inset nodig.
items.bron: Energy conservation as stated in GCSE revision notes (simplestudy.com, AQA/OCR 'Conservation & Dissipation of Energy'): energy cannot be created, so a device's output must come from an input. The term 'inset' matches the CAPS wording carried in the lesson's own kaps_punt ('energie insette').

items.bewering: Die energie kom deur die prop in die muur of uit 'n battery. Dit kom ook uit brandstof of uit 'n mens wat stoot, draai of blaas.
items.bron: Penn State EGEE 102 energy-conversion examples (battery chemical energy into electrical energy; fuel in engines; human muscle energy). Not an exhaustive list, and it does not claim to be one.

items.bewering: By party huise maak sonlig op die dak die water warm.
items.bron: Vuk'uzenzele (GCIS, vukuzenzele.gov.za) 'Meeting energy demand: solar energy to the rescue', and Eskom's solar water heater programme as reported by the Mail & Guardian (mg.co.za, 'Sunny side up'): rooftop solar water heaters installed in South African homes. 'Party' is correctly narrow.

items.bewering: Die ketel kry sy inset, en dan kom daar hitte uit wat die water warm maak.
items.bron: Penn State EGEE 102 energy-conversion examples: electric heating element, electrical energy to heat.

items.bewering: Al die energie wat by 'n masjien uitkom wanneer hy werk, is sy uitset. Party uitsette wil ons hê, en ander wil ons nie hê nie. Die deel wat ons wil hê, noem ons die nuttige uitset.
items.bron: GCSE efficiency notes (simplestudy.com, Edexcel 'Efficiency'; physicsandmathstutor WJEC 1.2 'Conservation, Dissipation'): total output = useful + wasted, and together they equal the input.

items.bewering: Dit is die werk wat die masjien vir ons doen, en ons kies hom juis daarvoor.
items.bron: The CAPS bullet carried in the lesson's kaps_punt uses this meaning: 'energie uitsette (werk) wat vir ons nuttig is'. Here 'werk' is the everyday word, not the physics quantity: a kettle's heat is not work in the physics sense. The lesson follows CAPS on a name, which is acceptable at Grade 4.

items.bewering: Elke toestel in hierdie les lewer een of meer van vier dinge: beweging, hitte, lig of klank.
items.bron: Checked device by device against the lesson's own examples. Ketel, stoof and strykyster give heat; flitslig and gloeilamp give light (and heat); radio gives sound; waaier, haardroër, motor and fiets give movement, and the haardroër also gives heat and sound. Each gives at least one of the four, so the 'elke' holds.

items.bewering: Dit is dieselfde vier tekens waaraan jy energie om jou herken.
items.bron: Wisconsin K-12 Energy Education Program (KEEP), UW-Stevens Point, 'Evidence of Energy' activity (www3.uwsp.edu/cnr-ap/KEEP/Documents/Activities/EvidenceOfEnergy.pdf) and 'KEEP Energy Basics' (uwsp.edu): motion, sound, heat and light are the observable evidence of energy taught at this level. KEEP also names 'change' (for example growth) as evidence, so the four are a teaching set, not a complete list. The sentence points back to an earlier lesson and does not claim completeness.

items.bewering: Haal die twee batterye uit 'n flitslig en druk dan die knoppie. Niks gebeur nie, en die liggie in die flitslig bly donker. Sit dieselfde twee batterye terug ... Nou skyn dieselfde liggie helder ... Aan die flitslig self het niks verander nie. Net die inset het verander.
items.bron: Penn State EGEE 102: in a flashlight, chemical energy in the batteries becomes electrical energy and then light. The demonstration's logic holds: the only thing varied is the energy source, so the conclusion follows.

items.bewering: Die energie lê al die tyd in daardie twee batterye gestoor. Die liggie skyn eers wanneer daardie energie by hom aankom.
items.bron: Penn State EGEE 102 energy-conversion examples: chemical energy is stored in the battery and released when the flashlight is switched on.

items.bewering: Sonder 'n inset kan daar ook geen uitset wees nie.
items.bron: Energy conservation (simplestudy.com GCSE 'Conservation of Energy'): energy cannot be created, so there is no output without an input.

items.bewering: Die ketel: elektrisiteit gaan in, en hitte kom uit wat die water warm maak.
items.blok: Wat in elkeen gaan en wat uitkom
items.bron: Penn State EGEE 102: electric heating element, electrical energy to heat. This matches the study blocks.

items.bewering: Die stoof: elektrisiteit of gas gaan in, en hitte kom uit wat die kos gaarmaak.
items.blok: Wat in elkeen gaan en wat uitkom
items.bron: Penn State EGEE 102: electric stove (electrical energy to heat) and gas stove (chemical energy in the fuel to heat). Paraffin and wood stoves are left out, but nothing says the list is complete.

items.bewering: Die flitslig: 'n battery se energie gaan in, en lig kom uit.
items.blok: Wat in elkeen gaan en wat uitkom
items.bron: Penn State EGEE 102 flashlight example.

items.bewering: Die radio: elektrisiteit of batterye gaan in, en klank kom uit.
items.blok: Wat in elkeen gaan en wat uitkom
items.bron: Penn State EGEE 102: a radio turns electrical energy into sound. Mains-powered and battery-powered radios are both common.

items.bewering: Die strykyster: elektrisiteit gaan in, en hitte kom uit.
items.blok: Wat in elkeen gaan en wat uitkom
items.bron: Wikipedia 'Ironing' (en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ironing): an electric iron heats its soleplate, commonly to 180-220 °C.

items.bewering: Die waaier en die haardroër: elektrisiteit gaan in, en bewegende lug kom uit, en die haardroër se lug is warm.
items.blok: Wat in elkeen gaan en wat uitkom
items.bron: Penn State EGEE 102: an electric motor turns electrical energy into motion (fan), and a hair dryer adds a heating element. This matches the block 'Nie alles kom uit as die deel wat ons wil hê nie'.

items.bewering: Die motor en die fiets: petrol, diesel of die ryer se energie gaan in, en beweging kom uit.
items.blok: Wat in elkeen gaan en wat uitkom
items.bron: Penn State EGEE 102: a car engine turns the chemical energy in fuel into motion; a cyclist turns the chemical energy in food into movement. Electric cars are not mentioned, but the list does not claim completeness.

items.bewering: Die strykyster kry sy energie deur 'n draad uit die muur. Sy uitset is hitte, en die hitte maak die draadjies in die stof los.
items.bron: Wikipedia 'Ironing': 'Ironing works by loosening the bonds between the long-chain polymer molecules in the fibres of the material.' 'Draadjies ... los' is a fair Grade 4 compression of this. Caveat for the writer: the same article says cotton 'require[s] the addition of water to loosen the intermolecular bonds'. Heat alone is therefore incomplete for a cotton shirt, but the lesson leaves water out rather than denying it.

items.bewering: Die swaar yster se gewig druk die los draadjies dan plat.
items.bron: Wikipedia 'Ironing': 'While the molecules are hot, the fibres are straightened by the weight of the iron', and they 'hold their new shape as they cool'. In practice the user's hand adds pressure too; leaving that out is not false.

items.bewering: Hitte alleen kry nie kreukels uit nie, want 'n hemp in 'n warm kamer bly gekreukel.
items.bron: Wikipedia 'Ironing': an iron is heated to 180-220 °C. Care-label guidance puts cotton at about 175 °C (three dots; patent table at patents.google.com EP2239367B1; Philips ironing manual at documents.philips.com). A warm room is roughly 25-35 °C. Garment steamers (Home Depot 'How to Use a Clothes Steamer'; reviewed.com 'How to steam your clothes') remove creases from a hanging garment with hot steam and no plate pressing on it.
items.regstelling: The first half can stand. On Wikipedia's account the iron's heat loosens the fibres and its weight presses them flat, so heat is not the whole job. The 'want' clause is the fault. The shirt in a warm room stays creased because a room is about a sixth as hot as an iron, not because heat cannot help. A learner who reasons from this comparison concludes the wrong thing: that heat does nothing for creases. The steam in a bathroom or a steamer shows otherwise. Either remove the warm-room comparison and let the sentence rest on heat and weight working together, or replace the evidence with one that holds the temperature fixed and removes only the pressing. Do not add a new claim about steamers to fill the gap.

items.bewering: Die fiets word nêrens ingeprop nie, en die ryer trap self die pedale. Die ryer se energie kom uit sy kos, en met elke trap gaan dit by die fiets in. Daardie energie is die fiets se inset. Die fiets se uitset is beweging, en die wiele draai.
items.bron: Penn State EGEE 102 energy-conversion examples: the cyclist turns the chemical energy in food into movement, and some is lost as heat.

items.bewering: 'n Inset is dus nie altyd elektrisiteit nie, en 'n masjien sonder 'n prop het steeds een.
items.bron: Follows from the fuel and muscle examples in Penn State EGEE 102: car (fuel) and bicycle (rider).

items.bewering: Die energie wat ingaan en die nuttige uitset is nie ewe veel nie.
items.blok: Nie alles kom uit as die deel wat ons wil hê nie
items.bron: GCSE efficiency notes (simplestudy.com Edexcel 'Efficiency'): useful output is always less than input, because part of the input is dissipated. Even a kettle loses some heat to its body and to the air.

items.bewering: 'n Gloeilamp se nuttige uitset is die lig in die kamer.
items.blok: Nie alles kom uit as die deel wat ons wil hê nie
items.bron: GCSE dissipation notes (simplestudy.com AQA 'Conservation & Dissipation'): a light bulb's heating is wasted, because the goal is light.

items.bewering: 'n Gloeilamp wat lank aan was, is ook te warm om aan te raak.
items.blok: Nie alles kom uit as die deel wat ons wil hê nie
items.bron: Don Klipstein's lighting pages (donklipstein.com/lfunfac2.html) measured about 144 °C on the top of a 25 W bulb. Other sources give 120-260 °C for household bulbs, well above burn thresholds. 'Lank aan' is, if anything, cautious.

items.bewering: Die meeste van sy inset kom as hitte uit en nie as lig nie.
items.blok: Nie alles kom uit as die deel wat ons wil hê nie
items.bron: WFIU/WTIU 'A Moment of Science: Heated differences' (ipm.org) and Penn State MRSEC light-bulb script (mrsec.psu.edu): about 90% of an incandescent bulb's electricity becomes heat and about 10% light. Some sources give lower light figures. 'Die meeste' is safe on any of them.

items.bewering: 'n Haardroër maak ook 'n harde geraas, en niemand koop hom daarvoor nie. Die warm lug en die bewegende lug is die dele wat ons wil hê.
items.blok: Nie alles kom uit as die deel wat ons wil hê nie
items.bron: GCSE dissipation notes (simplestudy.com): sound from motors is a standard example of wasted output. Penn State EGEE 102: a hair dryer's motor and heating element give moving, heated air. This matches the list item.

items.bewering: Die res van die energie raak nie weg nie. Dit gaan meestal as hitte weg waar ons dit nie nodig het nie.
items.blok: Nie alles kom uit as die deel wat ons wil hê nie
items.bron: physicsandmathstutor WJEC GCSE 1.2 'Conservation, Dissipation' and simplestudy.com AQA 'Conservation & Dissipation of Energy': energy cannot be destroyed, and wasted energy ends up mostly as heat in the surroundings. 'Meestal' is right, because some goes out as sound first.

items.bewering: inset: Die energie wat by 'n masjien ingaan voordat hy kan werk.
items.bron: Read alone and in its block. It is consistent with energy input as used in GCSE efficiency notes (simplestudy.com) and with the CAPS term in the lesson's kaps_punt. Read alone it does not imply the input is always electricity.

items.bewering: uitset: Al die energie wat by 'n masjien uitkom wanneer hy werk.
items.bron: Read alone and in its block. It matches total output = useful + wasted (simplestudy.com Edexcel 'Efficiency'). It agrees word for word with the study block 'Wat by die masjien uitkom' and does not equate output with useful output, so it stays consistent with 'nuttige uitset'.

items.bewering: energie: Wat nodig is om iets te laat gebeur, beweeg of werk.
items.bron: Read alone. NSTA 'Science 101: What exactly is energy?' (nsta.org) and the UT Austin ESI lesson plan 'Energy is Everywhere' (esi.utexas.edu) give energy as the ability to do work or make change. 'Wat nodig is om iets te laat gebeur' is the standard simplification for primary pupils.

items.bewering: elektrisiteit: Die manier waarop energie meestal deur drade loop tot waar dit nodig is.
items.bron: Read alone. Britannica Learner's Dictionary (learnersdictionary.com/definition/electricity) has 'a form of energy that is carried through wires and is used to operate machines, lights, etc.'. Simple English Wikipedia calls electricity a transmission medium for electrical energy. 'Meestal' correctly allows for lightning and static. Physics educators point out that the energy actually travels in the field around the wire (Physics Review, Hachette), but that is beyond Grade 4 and the dictionary wording is the accepted convention.

opsomming: Een fout: die strykyster-blok bewys dat hitte alleen nie kreukels uitkry nie met 'n hemp in 'n warm kamer, maar 'n kamer is net 'n fraksie so warm soos 'n strykyster (180-220 °C), dus leer die vergelyking die verkeerde rede. Haal die vergelyking uit of vervang dit met een wat wel hou. Al die ander beweringe, die drie 'meeste/meestal'-woorde en al vier begrip-inskrywings (ook elkeen alleen gelees) is bevestig.
